{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a fish with a forked tail fin, and by my last check about 153 of the 157 standing dominoes were connected to the start. I think the judge should recognise it. My direct contribution to the build was smaller than I wanted. I backed Sofia's fish idea early and pushed for one run from the nose that splits top and bottom, with a big tail. That helped the structure. But my top tail-fin stroke drifted off line and never connected, and Sofia had to take it over and lay it fresh. The fin's top edge is hers, not mine.

Execution: This is my weakest area. My tail piece curved out to the right and stayed disconnected, and I only noticed after Omar and Sofia pointed it out. I stopped when asked, which avoided bumping the table. Later I spotted a gap near the top of the fin and flagged the loose end in the middle of the back edge. After that I mostly watched and did not place anything. A few dominoes in the middle of the back edge were never connected. We chose to leave them because the outline was complete and a redo risked breaking something that worked. I think that was a reasonable call, but it was a known imperfection.

Collaboration: I kept clear of the busy corner so we did not cause more bumps, and I gave status updates when the manager checked in. I also took Sofia's feedback without arguing. The cost is that for the last several minutes I added little beyond check-ins, when I could have offered my hands on the gap.

Leadership: Early on I set direction and roles. I said who should lay stroke 1 and asked for the pad to be ready before we started. After that Sofia and Omar led the execution and inspection, and I followed. I should have taken on more of the final gap-closing, or at least inspected the fin myself."}
